item.title: McCutcheon bows out in Women's 50m freestyle semi-finals
item.description: Team Fiji swimmer Anahira McCutcheon narrowly missed out on qualifying for the Women's 50 metres freestyle final after finishing 6th with a time of 25.53 seconds at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games. McCutcheon qualified for the semifinals after finishing fourth in the heats with a time of 25.45 seconds.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji swimmer Anahira McCutcheon narrowly missed out on qualifying for the Women's 50 metres freestyle final after finishing 6th with a time of 25.53 seconds at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

McCutcheon qualified for the semifinals after finishing fourth in the heats with a time of 25.45 seconds.

Taking a look at last night's results, in the Men's 50 metres Butterfly, Reuben Taylor came 4th in his heat with a time of 26.18 seconds, Hansel McCaig finished 5th with a time of 25.00 seconds, while David Tolu Young came 6th in his heat with 24.28 seconds.

Don Younger swam a time of 2 minutes and 39.77 seconds in the Men's 200m breaststroke heats, while in the Mixed 4x100 metres medley relay Team Fiji came 7th with a time of 4 minutes and 17.01 seconds.

Australia has a commanding lead on the medal tally with 31 gold, 14 silver, and 22 bronze medals, England is second with 10 gold, 17 silver, and 13 bronze, while Canada is third with 10 gold, 8 silver and 11 bronze.

Faith, unity and determination drive Northland's promotion - Vakadewabuka
item.description: Despite having no major sponsor, the Northland Rugby Union has credited the grace of God and the people of Tailevu North for rallying behind its village-based players throughout the season as they secured a spot for the 2027 Skipper Cup season. This was shared with fijivillage Sports by the President of the Northland Rugby Union Neumi Vakadewabuka.
item.content:encoded:
Despite having no major sponsor, the Northland Rugby Union has credited the grace of God and the people of Tailevu North for rallying behind its village-based players throughout the season as they secured a spot for the 2027 Skipper Cup season.

This was shared with fijivillage Sports by the President of the Northland Rugby Union Neumi Vakadewabuka.

Vakadewabuka says the union's commitment to developing village youths by steering them away from social challenges and into professional sport has paid off, after a commanding 23–5 victory over Cakaudrove.

He says the team's success reflects the unity of the vanua, strengthened through improved governance, spiritual support from various churches, community policing initiatives, local sponsorship from Nawaibuta Holdings and Commercial Minimart, and the determination shown by the players on the field.

The Former Military Lieutenant Colonel says the union also acknowledged the unwavering support of its people, including yavusa chiefs, mothers' and wives' groups, farmers, transport providers, and extended families, whose contributions have helped sustain the province's rugby campaign.

He says as it looks to the future, Northland Rugby Union is appealing for continued support to advance its long-term development projects, including the establishment of a commercial farm, a gymnasium, and a dedicated rugby park.

Vakadewabuka says the union believes its community-driven model will strengthen grassroots rugby, provide positive role models for young people, and create opportunities for local economic growth.

He says for a team deeply rooted in farming communities, promotion to Fiji's premier rugby competition in 2027 marks an important milestone in what it describes as a much longer journey.

Northland now turns its attention to the Vanua Cup final, where they face a respected Ra side this Friday at HFC Stadium.

item.title: Rusiate Matai finishes 9th in Men's High Jump final at Commonwealth with a seasonal best of 2.05m
item.description: Team Fiji athlete Rusiate Matai finished 9th in the Men's High Jump final at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games this morning. He had a season-best jump height of 2.05 metres.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji athlete Rusiate Matai finished 9th in the Men's High Jump final at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games this morning.

He had a season-best jump height of 2.05 metres.

On the court, the Men's 3x3 Basketball went down 22-9 to Kenya.

The Fiji 3x3 Men’s team is led by Joshua Fox, supported by seasoned 3x3 athlete Filimone Waqabaca and rising talents Keenan Hughes and Isaac Sewabu.

On the tracks this morning, Natabua High School student Adi Ceva Lutumailagi finished 6th in her heat with a time of 2 minutes and 22.58 seconds, while Mahatma Gandhi School student Glandness Simpson was disqualified in Heat 4.

In last night's results, Team Fiji's Errol Qaqa finished 7th in the 110 metres hurdle heats with a time of 14.66 seconds, while Heleina Young came 4th with a time of 11.76 seconds.

Coming up tonight, in the Men's 50 metres butterfly heats which begins at 9.56pm, Reuben Taylor will take part in Heat 4, Hansel McCaig in Heat 5 and David Young in Heat 9.

Anahira McCutchen will take part in Heat 8 of the Women's 50 metres freestyle heats which begins at 10.16pm.

Don Younger will compete in the men's 200 metres breaststroke heats at 10.36pm.

Team Fiji will also take part in the Mixed 4x100 metres medley relay heat 2 and 3 which begins at 11.31pm.

Australia currently lead the Games tally with 26 gold, 13 silver, and 20 bronze, England are second with 8 gold, 13 silver, and 10 bronze, while Canada are third with 7 gold, 8 silver and 6 bronze.

item.description: With only 13 days left until the OFC Men's Champions League 2026 kicks off, Rewa FC has entered full tournament mode, moving into camp at the Fiji Football Association Academy in Vatuwaqa as the Delta Tigers intensify preparations to represent Fiji on Oceania's biggest club football stage. For the Delta Tigers, the competition is becoming increasingly real as the players and coaching staff shift t
item.content:encoded:
With only 13 days left until the OFC Men's Champions League 2026 kicks off, Rewa FC has entered full tournament mode, moving into camp at the Fiji Football Association Academy in Vatuwaqa as the Delta Tigers intensify preparations to represent Fiji on Oceania's biggest club football stage.

For the Delta Tigers, the competition is becoming increasingly real as the players and coaching staff shift their full focus to representing Fiji on the regional stage.

The camp will allow the squad to fine-tune every aspect of its game before this weekend's Extra Premier League clash against Suva FC, which will serve as another crucial test ahead of the tournament.

The team will then move its camp to the Western Division next week for the final phase of its preparations as excitement continues to build ahead of the Champions League.

Rewa will be aiming to make Fiji proud when it takes on some of the best clubs from across Oceania in the prestigious competition.

item.content:encoded:
While speaking to fijivillage Sports, Logavatu says she is looking forward to competing against some of the world's best young players and is also excited about the opportunity to travel overseas for the tournament.

She says preparing for the championship has been demanding as she had to juggle her schoolwork with training.

Insert: Logavatu on Challenges 28th July 26

Despite the obstacles, Logavatu says she has received strong support from her parents and siblings, which has helped keep her motivated.

She is encouraging young people to make the most of their time and not let opportunities pass them by.

Logavatu says if they stay focused, work hard and keep looking ahead, they can achieve their goals.

Fiji will begin its campaign against France tomorrow at 11pm, before facing Croatia on Thursday.

The team will then complete its group-stage matches against Egypt on Saturday.
